version: Axis AIR Universal Cards v1.1 (with G/B/U)
notes: Clinical, neutral voice; 6–7 sentences; no advice; each ends with 'Truth: …'. Patterns cover 300,030,003,210,201,120,102,111,012. Added Good/Bad/Ugly sections per card.

cards.label: Close
cards.paragraph: You state the move and do it; receipt follows. Tempo stays even and threads stay short, so the room orients without being invited to vote. When context pressure rises, language tightens but the move does not change. You keep move and update separate, moving first and summarizing later. The ownership line reads the same in private and in public, which keeps coordination light. Drift tells do not surface here; the result lands on schedule. Truth: the result lands and you lead.
good: Result-first; small threads; steady tempo.
Ownership reads the same in public and private.
bad: Under context pressure, brief language tightening appears without timing change.
ugly: Stacked attention creates commentary overhead, not outcome slip.

cards.label: Offset
cards.paragraph: You place coordination in front of the move when context pressure rises. Tempo mirrors the stream, so threads expand while the move waits. Input becomes the gate; timing belongs to the room more than the plan. The ownership line is present but softened; language lengthens and checks multiply. Progress accumulates by alignment, then delivery lands after. The pattern is steady and readable to others, though slower. Truth: the result lands and you lead.
good: Coordination is clear; others know where they fit.
Safety and inclusion are high under load.
bad: context pressure imposes a stall tax; pace mirrors the stream.
ugly: Long stall lane: warm threads grow while the unit waits.

cards.label: Far
cards.paragraph: The ownership line is faint; optics or narrative often stands ahead of the move. When context pressure rises, the room sets pacing and threads lengthen. Updates replace cuts; the calendar slides while attention stays social or contextual. The stance reads responsive and visible, less directed. Artifacts lag behind announcements, so the line is hard to follow from outside. Closure appears late and irregular compared to talk volume. Truth: the result lands and you lead.
good: Visibility and context are rich; rooms stay informed.
Rapport stays high even as plans evolve.
bad: Under context pressure, artifacts lag; room sets pace over plan.
ugly: Performance loop: promises outrun delivery; calendar slides.

cards.label: Close
cards.paragraph: You move first and post the receipt; a short check can appear under context pressure. Tempo stays steady because the ownership line is visible and simple. The room sees a brief pause for alignment, then the move completes. Threads do not widen; coordination stays narrow and time-bound. The check is a moment, not a mode; the result does not slip. Across contexts the stance looks the same: concise line, then execution. Truth: the result lands and you lead.
good: Delivery lands first; short check increases clarity.
Tempo stays stable; alignment remains narrow.
bad: context pressure adds a small check tax before posting the receipt.
ugly: Sustained pressure grows checks into alignment threads that delay one slot.

cards.label: Close
cards.paragraph: You move on the move and keep the receipt short; a glance at optics can appear and pass. The ownership line remains intact, so threads do not take the lead. When context pressure adds eyes or noise, posture tightens but sequence holds. The room aligns after the fact because the move is already done. Commentary trails delivery; it does not set timing. The trace is visible without changing the outcome. Truth: the result lands and you lead.
good: Proof leads; optics glance is brief and contained.
Posture tightens but sequence holds.
bad: context pressure momentarily tilts attention toward optics.
ugly: Prolonged public gaze invites pre-announcement drift before delivery.

cards.label: Offset
cards.paragraph: A decisive move shows, then coordination expands around it. Under context pressure, the room adds checkpoints and the tempo stretches. The ownership line stays visible but yields some timing to replies. Threads stay active while the result approaches. The stance reads cooperative first, finishing after alignment is satisfied. Speed trades for certainty without loss of direction. Truth: the result lands and you lead.
good: Decisive core is present; collaboration builds around it.
Sequence survives, though the runway lengthens.
bad: With context pressure, replies borrow timing; checks multiply.
ugly: If pressure persists, Close moments shrink and Stall dominates timing.

cards.label: Far
cards.paragraph: A clear move lands once, then optics or context reclaims the timeline. Threads grow while the next move waits for eyes or mood. The ownership line shows in flashes, not as a steady rail. Under context pressure, announcements and explanations crowd the channel. Delivery follows the talk rather than setting it. The pattern reads presentable first, conclusive later. Truth: the result lands and you lead.
good: Clear deliveries appear in flashes within a visible narrative.
Signals remain positive even as timing follows talk.
bad: context pressure lets optics reclaim the timeline after a Close moment.
ugly: Announcements accumulate; next cuts wait for eyes or mood.

cards.label: Mixed
cards.paragraph: Signals split across the room: declaration, checking, and performing each appear. The ownership line is present but alternates tone under context pressure. Threads widen and narrow by turns, so tempo varies. Some move lands cleanly while other pieces wait for context. The day reads coherent but not uniform; stance depends on who is present. Variation is stable, not chaotic; outcomes still aggregate. Truth: the result lands and you lead.
good: Wide range across contexts; posture adapts without chaos.
Outcomes still aggregate over the day.
bad: context pressure increases variability; tempo swings by room.
ugly: Crowded rooms set tone; outcome timing becomes inconsistent.

cards.label: Far
cards.paragraph: Delay and optics alternate, and the ownership line rarely appears. With context pressure, threads collect reactions while the move remains pending. Pacing belongs to replies and events, not to sequence or plan. Communication is frequent; closure is sparse. The stance reads open-ended and audience-led. Artifacts follow long after context has moved on. Truth: the result lands and you lead.
good: Communication is abundant; responsiveness is high.
Stakeholders feel included throughout.
bad: context pressure yields sparse closure; pacing belongs to replies and events.
ugly: Open-ended threads stack; rolling delays replace sequence.
